solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Start to concentrate before bishop leads meeting in intellectual manner (10)

indicators.note: the start of 'concentrate' is its first letter, C
whatever leads goes in front, so the bishop's letter heads the meeting word

blocks.note: a rally is a mass meeting

annotation.surface: Advice to a thinker: focus first, then let the bishop chair the meeting in a suitably brainy way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Before' is not a positional instruction but a word in its own right, the old poetic synonym; only 'leads' does any placing.
annotation.definitionFit: Cerebral means of the intellect, so cerebrally is doing something in an intellectual manner.

entries.clue: Composer using four notes — or none! (4)

blocks.note: C, A, G and E are all musical notes
surface padding: a joke about the composer's silent piece

annotation.surface: A composer whose tune needs only four notes, or even no notes at all.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Or none!' is a joke rather than wordplay: John Cage's most famous piece, 4'33", is four and a half minutes in which the performer plays nothing.
annotation.definitionFit: John Cage was the American avant-garde composer.

entries.clue: Money that is held by opposing sides (4)

indicators.note: IE is held inside R and L

blocks.note: right and left, opposite sides; splits as R...L

annotation.surface: Cash that is clutched between two sides in a dispute.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Opposing sides' sounds like two teams or parties; it is just right and left.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Cambodia's currency unit, divided into 100 sen.

entries.clue: French mathematician developed basis with Laplace (6,6)

indicators.note: the letters are worked up into a new form

annotation.surface: A French mathematician built his theory on foundations laid alongside Laplace.
annotation.walkthrough: Laplace, himself a French mathematician, is a decoy for the answer and merely supplies letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Blaise Pascal, 17th-century French mathematician of Pascal's triangle.

entries.clue: Fine instrument used in dramatisation (5)

indicators.note: the answer is found in use inside the next word

blocks.note: the answer sits in letters three to seven of this word

annotation.surface: A fine instrument features in a stage production.
annotation.walkthrough: An Amati is a violin made by the Amati family of Cremona, forerunners of Stradivari.
annotation.definitionFit: Amati violins are prized instruments, so 'fine' is fair.

entries.clue: Story about female underwear I start to read in bookshop abroad (9)

indicators.note: LIE goes around the other pieces
the start of 'read' is its first letter, R

blocks.note: a story is a lie, as in 'don't tell stories'; splits as LI...E
I, then the first letter of 'read'; the printed clue supplies only one I, so it has to serve twice

annotation.surface: A racy story about lingerie is the first thing one picks up in a foreign bookshop.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue is flawed, as the Times editor acknowledged: the printed wording accounts for one I too few, so the answer needs a letter the clue never supplies.
annotation.definitionFit: Librairie is French for a bookshop, so 'abroad' flags the foreign word.

entries.clue: Bird lives on Irish beaches primarily (4)

indicators.note: take the first letter of 'beaches'
in an across clue, to be 'on' something is to come after it, so the verb follows

annotation.surface: A bird that makes its home mostly on the beaches of Ireland.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lives' is a verb, the plain 'is' of existence, not the plural of life.
annotation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-billed wading bird.

entries.clue: For instance, net something no longer deemed fashionable? (4-6)

blocks.note: net written backwards spells a number word
a person or thing that is out of date, like an old magazine issue

annotation.surface: A fishing net, say, is something that has gone out of fashion.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic riddle: NET is TEN written back to front, so it is literally a number backwards, a 'back number'.
annotation.definitionFit: A back number is an old issue of a periodical, hence anyone or anything out of date.

entries.clue: Parable I utilised in original way to convey meaning primarily (10)

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged in a novel, original fashion
take the first letter of 'meaning'

blocks.note: first letter, added to the mix

annotation.surface: A storyteller explaining how they used a parable in a fresh way to put their point across.
annotation.walkthrough: The M from 'meaning' joins the anagram rather than sitting outside it.
annotation.definitionFit: Similitude is an old word for a comparison or allegory, so a parable.

entries.clue: Actress to feel bad about taking off a dress — nothing to finish with! (5,5)

indicators.note: RE is taken off the front of REGRET
the zero comes at the finish, as the last piece of the answer

blocks.note: to regret something is to feel bad about it

annotation.surface: An actress regretting that she took off a dress and has nothing left to wear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Feel bad about' reads as one phrase, but 'about' is split off to be removed, the usual 'concerning' abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was the Swedish-born Hollywood star.

entries.clue: Trick rogue, quietly departing (4)

indicators.note: departing means leaving, so the letter walks out of the word

blocks.note: P = piano, quietly in music; removed

annotation.surface: A rogue slipping away silently after pulling a trick.
annotation.walkthrough: P for piano is the musical marking for quiet.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a scam is a con, a dishonest trick for money.

entries.clue: Legislation brought by British, bad old folk not looking good (4,2,6)

blocks.note: a fright is an unsightly person, as in 'you look a fright'

annotation.surface: A law passed by the British against wicked, unattractive old people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bad old folk' looks like one unit, but it breaks into ILL, O and the FRIGHTS who are not looking good.
annotation.definitionFit: The Bill of Rights is the 1689 English statute, and the US amendments, both legislation.

entries.clue: A small number helping almost everyone having high hopes (12)

indicators.note: ALL loses its last letter

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels
a ration is a helping or portion

annotation.surface: A small group of helpers, nearly all of them full of ambition.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A small number' reads as a few people, but splits into A, S and PI.
annotation.definitionFit: Aspirational describes someone with aspirations, hoping to rise.

entries.clue: At rest, so we abandoned cars (3-7)

indicators.note: the letters are thrown about with abandon

annotation.surface: Parked and still, the cars had been left behind by their owners.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned cars' is such a natural phrase that 'abandoned' hides its job; here it means wild, without restraint.
annotation.definitionFit: Two-seaters are small cars with room for only two.

entries.clue: Change still perceived as feature of church (10)

indicators.note: to be perceived is to be taken in by the senses, here by the listening ear

annotation.surface: A sign that change is still regarded as part of church life.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still' is a noun here, as in 'the still of the night', giving PEACE rather than 'yet'.
annotation.definitionFit: An altarpiece is the painting or carving behind a church altar.

entries.clue: Poet Edmund eats soft food that comes in rolls (9)

annotation.definitionNote: a relative clause standing for a noun: something that comes in rolls

indicators.note: WALLER takes PAP inside him

blocks.note: Edmund Waller, 17th-century English poet; splits as WALL...ER

annotation.surface: A poet eating mush, with 'food that comes in rolls' suggesting bread.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Food that comes in rolls' looks like bread; the definition is only 'that comes in rolls', and the food is the PAP.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the decorator's paper is sold wound on rolls, which is what the clue points to.

entries.clue: Right to graze cattle in former city once upon a time (9)

indicators.note: 'in' puts one thing inside another, so the city sits within the phrase for olden days

blocks.note: a past age, splits as PAST...AGE

annotation.surface: An ancient grazing right from a long-vanished city.
annotation.walkthrough: Ur of the Chaldees is the crossword's favourite ancient city.
annotation.definitionFit: Pasturage is pasture land and, in law, the right to graze animals on it.

entries.clue: Restrict learner with self-aggrandizing boast (5)

blocks.note: 'I'm it', claiming to be the top person

annotation.surface: Rein in the learner driver who keeps bragging.
annotation.walkthrough: I'M IT is the boast of someone who thinks they are the best.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to limit something is to keep it within set bounds, to restrict it.

entries.clue: Examinations of small vessel within bigger one (5)

indicators.note: within means inside, so the small vessel is placed inside the bigger one's letters

blocks.note: SS = steamship, a bigger vessel; splits as S...S
a can is a small container

annotation.surface: Inspections of a small boat carried aboard a larger ship.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' is a ship on the surface but a container for CAN, while the bigger vessel really is a ship.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a scan is a close look, whether by a radiographer or an eye running over a page.

entries.clue: City halved effort to stop protection (9)

indicators.note: only the first half of 'effort' is used
EFF stops up SHIELD, sitting inside it

blocks.note: a shield is protection; splits as SH...IELD

annotation.surface: A city's defences weakened because its protection effort was cut in half.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Halved' belongs to 'effort', not to 'City'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the South Yorkshire city famous for steel and cutlery.

entries.clue: Human replica evolved like characters in Fahrenheit 451? (12)

indicators.note: the letters change into a new form

annotation.surface: A science-fiction scenario of an evolving android in Ray Bradbury's dystopia.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Characters in Fahrenheit 451' suggests the people in Bradbury's novel; it means the printed characters of the title, letters and digits.
annotation.definitionFit: The title mixes letters and numbers, which is what alphanumeric means.

entries.clue: One apprehended by journalist with court order (5)

indicators.note: I is caught inside ED...CT

blocks.note: CT = court, as in street names

annotation.surface: Someone arrested by a reporter who carries a court order.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Court order' looks like the definition, but 'court' is CT and only 'order' defines.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a decree issued by a ruler or authority is a command, an order.

entries.clue: Particle of meat, not dry (4)

indicators.note: 'not dry' asks for the meat without its dry element, so those letters are simply dropped

annotation.surface: A scrap of meat that has not been dried.
annotation.walkthrough: TT is teetotal: a dry person drinks no alcohol.
annotation.definitionFit: The muon is a subatomic particle, a heavy cousin of the electron.

entries.clue: Party’s set up something to eat (4)

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means written upwards

blocks.note: the DUP, Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party, plus 's

annotation.surface: A political party has laid on some food.
annotation.walkthrough: The DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party, and the 's joins it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the informal word means a potato, which is certainly something to eat.

entries.clue: English lord failing to keep right sword (4)

indicators.note: PEER does not hold on to its R

annotation.surface: An English nobleman losing his grip on his rightful sword.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Failing to keep' drops a letter rather than a possession.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one of the three weapons of modern fencing, the heaviest, is a sword.

entries.clue: Foreign capital quietly blocking raised matter of only local interest (6-4)

indicators.note: P blocks HUMP, sitting inside it

blocks.note: a hump is a raised mass; splits as H...UMP

annotation.surface: Something in a far-off capital is obstructing a matter that only concerns locals.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Raised matter' sounds like an issue brought up; it is a physical lump, a HUMP.
annotation.definitionFit: Parish-pump politics are petty and parochial, like gossip round the village pump.

entries.clue: Killed a large number (4)

blocks.note: an informal noun, originally American, for a great many

annotation.surface: Many people were killed.
annotation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase, it sounds like a massacre; it is two separate meanings.
annotation.definitionFit: Slew is the past tense of slay, and also an informal word for a great many.

entries.clue: Ditched plane caught side on in crash (10)

indicators.note: caught by the ear, as in 'I caught what you said'
the letters are smashed up

blocks.note: jet = plane; JETT is said the same way

annotation.surface: A plane hit side-on in a crash had to be ditched.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ditched plane' reads as an aircraft landing on water, but 'Ditched' alone defines. The extra T is justified only by sound, JETT being heard as JET.
annotation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw overboard or ditch.
